label: prop:unified-iterative-correction
title: Unified iterative LP-dual correction: per-step Wedderburn projection over all partitions $\lambda \vdash k$ for $k = 2, \ldots, K$, starting at $A = 1$ (no special cases)
html:
Proposition. Unified iterative LP-dual correction: per-step Wedderburn projection over all partitions \lambda \vdash k for k = 2, \ldots, K, starting at A = 1 (no special cases)

The unified iterative correction accumulates binding energy sequentially over the Young seminormal trace. For a partition \lambda \vdash k write

  u_\lambda \;=\; \frac{w_\lambda}{d_\lambda} \;-\; \frac{1}{[k]_q!},
  \qquad
  \varrho_\lambda(s) \;=\; \frac{1}{\mu_\lambda + s},
  \qquad
  s_\ast \;=\; \frac{q_0 - 1}{q_0},

where w_\lambda is the q-deformed Wedderburn weight, d_\lambda = \dim V_\lambda, and \mu_\lambda = \sum_{\square \in \lambda} [c(\square)]_q\,[c(\square)+1]_q is the Jucys–Murphy q-Casimir eigenvalue on the \lambda-block, so that \varrho_\lambda is the q-resolvent evaluated at the Planck-step Reeb frequency s_\ast. The per-partition contribution is

  B_\lambda(Z, N)
  = m_e \cdot H_q(\lambda) \cdot u_\lambda \cdot \varrho_\lambda(s_\ast) \cdot
    \big( \ln\big| \mathrm{tr}\, \mathbf{M}_\lambda^{(0..A)} \big| -
          \ln d_\lambda \big),

and the total unified correction is the sum of B_\lambda(Z, N) over every enumerated \lambda.

Only multi-dimensional mixing partitions carry a non-zero u_\lambda: the subtrahend 1/[k]_q! is exactly \min_\lambda (w_\lambda / d_\lambda), so it annihilates the two one-dimensional blocks (k) and (1^k) at every level and nothing else.

The formulation bypasses special-case branching entirely. Each atomic step computes an independent energy increment from the transition trace difference, and the increments telescope, so the per-partition total depends on the running product only through its final trace. The process extracts the binding increment via identical algebraic mechanisms across all values of A.

The selection rule that was removed

The sum above is unrestricted. Earlier formulations restricted it to those \lambda with \mathrm{tr}\, \mathbf{M}_\lambda^{(0..A)} \le 0. That restriction was asserted, not derived — it was what the accumulator computed rather than a consequence of the constraint it was named for — and it has been removed on that ground. Its status is fixed by the following.

Complementary slackness for a Frobenius positivity constraint \langle \Phi, \pi_\lambda \rangle \ge 0 makes tight mean \mathrm{tr} = 0, not \mathrm{tr} \le 0. Under that reading every selected block contributes the same constant and the total reads nothing about the nucleus; the selected set also meets the domain of \ln|\cdot| nowhere. Both are recorded in QOU.MassTheory.UICFunctionalSelection (uicGated_cs_eq, cs_selection_excludes_log_domain).

The operator-selection programme is degenerate as well: its net-constraint dual vanishes identically (QOU.ParticleInteractions.y_0_eq_zero_of_radical) and its minimiser set is a positive-dimensional face, so complementary slackness on that programme cannot single out a partition set at all.

Nor was the restriction a perturbation. Summing over all \lambda instead gives a total larger by a factor of 1.93 at A = 2 and 1.95 at A = 4, evaluated at the production truncation k_{\mathrm{exact}} = 11; at k_{\mathrm{exact}} = 4 the same two factors are 4.60 and 3.40. The quantity is strongly truncation-dependent — the unrestricted A = 2 total spans a factor of 43 across k_{\mathrm{exact}} = 4 \ldots 11 — so neither factor means anything quoted without its tier. The two readings coincide only when the excluded blocks happen to cancel exactly (uicGated_eq_uicAll_iff).

Removing the restriction is not an accuracy improvement. At A = 2 the AME2020 binding is +2.2246\;\mathrm{MeV}, and the restricted and unrestricted totals are both negative, the unrestricted one lying further from the measured value. What the removal discards is a selection step whose stated justification is false, not a term that was bringing the prediction closer to the data.

The name u_\lambda is a per-partition weight in closed form. It is not a shadow price of any programme — it is not the net-constraint dual, which vanishes, and at H_3 it is (0,\,0.16695,\,0) against the partition-indexed Frobenius duals (1,\,1,\,0) of the mass-coefficient block. It is written y_\lambda in the compute, where it is evaluated by hecke_core_legacy.lp_shadow_price; that name is historical and is not the Markov partition weight of the same glyph.
